newsitem.title: LEBANON: Merrill Lynch plans to expand Lebanon operation.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch plans to expand Lebanon operation.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said that it plans to expand its private banking operations in Lebanon, which it said has a lot of investment opportunities to offer to global investors.

The securities firm said it expects to increase its Beirut staff from 25 to 42 within the next 12 months. Since the end of 1995, when it moved into a new office in Beirut, Merrill Lynch has more than doubled the number of its employees in Lebanon.

"We aim to expand more and more in Lebanon. We want to reach to about 42 people in this office, experts in investment and investment vehicles and financial advisors who can give investment services to our clients in Lebanon and the region," John Dagher, Managing Director Merrill Lynch Lebanon, said.
"Also they can be a link between the Lebanese investor and the global investor and vice versa and with world markets and vice versa," he told a news conference.
Merrill Lynch, which has offices in 45 countries, is one of the largest securities firms in the world with private client assets of some $850 billion.

It lead-managed and arranged some $1 billion in debt and equity issues by the Lebanese government and banks since 1994, including Lebanon's highly successful $400 million Eurobond in October 1994 -- the first sovereign issue in the Middle East.

Andreas Berghendahl, co-head Global Debt Origination Merrill Lynch, said that with the U.S. and other stock markets highly valued, and interest rates and credit spreads very low, fixed income and equity investors are looking to tap other markets.
"I think this explains why these investors today are looking with a great deal of excitement and in a very positive way at the development in Lebanon," he told the conference.

"The country is going through an extremely exciting and positive development at this point, very strong redevelopment and rebuilding that provides for very exciting opportunities for international investors," Berghendahl added.

Alan Albert, senior managing director Merrill Lynch Global Asset Management, said that from an investment point of view the the Lebanese economy is at a very similar development stage to the Asian markets 10 or 15 years ago.

"There is still much to be done in terms of motivating and encouraging certain sectors like services but progress is being made and this is just the sort of opportunity that global investors are looking for," Albert said.

"The limitation at the moment is that this is still a small capitalised market. Global investors would like more availability of both bonds and equities in which they can invest their funds," he said.

"We are actively encourgaing investors to look at this area, we are actually looking here ourselves and we already have money invested in the area and clearly are following developments very, very closely," he added.
